title: Market-Implied Isotonic Calibration Baseline — Close-Moneyline as Calibration Anchor

source_research.title: Uncertainty-Aware Machine Learning for NBA Forecasting in Digital Betting Markets
source_research.key_finding: Market-only model (isotonic-regression calibration of closing moneyline implied probs) represents the best-possible probabilistic forecaster using only market information. LR baseline Brier=0.199 (tabular best).
source_research.action: Treat market-implied probability as calibration anchor — isotonic regression from model raw → market-calibrated

source_research.title: Stacked ensemble model for NBA game outcome prediction analysis
source_research.key_finding: Stacking with calibrated LR meta-learner. Feature importance: Elo diff, rolling win%, home court, recent margin consistently top.

source_research.title: Machine Learning for Basketball Game Outcomes: NBA and WNBA Leagues
source_research.key_finding: Logistic regression best Brier 0.199 / log-loss 0.583 on tabular baselines. XGBoost: Brier 0.202, higher AUC. Random Forest competitive on calibration.

hypothesis: Our GA-selected trees produce well-ranked probabilities but poorly calibrated. The literature shows two calibration paths that outperform our current lr_platt/venn_abers approach: (1) Isotonic regression against market-implied closing lines — this is the 'best possible' calibration since markets aggregate all public info; (2) LR as a final meta-learner trained on GA predictions + market features. Implementing (1) as a post-processing step could reduce Brier by 0.003-0.008.

implementation.approach: Two-stage calibration: tree GA prediction → isotonic → market-anchored output

stage_2.description: Isotonic regression trained on (p_model, market_implied) pairs from historical data
stage_2.training: Use trailing 200 games of (raw_model_prob, market_implied_prob, actual_outcome) triples
stage_2.rationale: Markets embed Elo, injuries, travel, public sentiment — all info not in our features
